title: Classification Based on Association Rules
text: Maintainer: Michael Hahsler R package arulesCBA (Hahsler et al. 2019) extension package arules (Hahsler et al. 2005) perform association rule-based classification. package provides infrastructure class association rules implements associative classifiers based following algorithms: CBA: Classification Based Association Rules (Liu et al. 1998). CMAR: Classification based Multiple Association Rules (Li et al. 2001) via LUCS-KDD Software Library. CPAR: Classification based Predictive Association Rules (Yin Han 2003) via LUCS-KDD Software Library. C4.5: Rules extracted C4.5 decision tree (Quinlan 1993) via J48 R/Weka. FOIL: First-Order Inductive Learner (Quinlan Cameron-Jones 1993; Yin Han 2003). PART: Rules Partial Decision Trees (Frank Witten 1998) via R/Weka. PRM: Predictive Rule Mining (Yin Han 2003) via LUCS-KDD Software Library. RCAR: Regularized Class Association Rules using Logistic Regression (Azmi et al. 2019). RIPPER: Repeated Incremental Pruning Produce Error Reduction (Cohen 1995) via R/Weka. package also provides infrastructure associative classification (supervised discretization mining class association rules (CARs)) implements various association rule-based classification strategies (first match, majority voting, weighted voting, etc.). algorithms interfaced R package R/Weka (Hornik et al. 2009) LUCS-KDD Software Library (Coenen 2013). following R packages use arulesCBA: arules, qCBA, tidybins

text: Class association rules (CARs) form $$P \Rightarrow c_i,$$ LHS \(P\) pattern (.e., itemset) \(c_i\) single item representing class label. Mining parameters. Mining parameters arules::apriori() can either specified list (object arules::APparameter) argument parameter , convenience, arguments .... Note: mineCARs() uses default minimum support 0.1 (LHS rules via parameter originalSupport = FALSE), minimum confidence 0.5 maxlen (rule length including items LHS RHS) 5. Balancing minimum support. Using single minimum support threshold highly imbalanced dataset can leave minority classes represented rules. address issue, balanceSupport = TRUE adjusts minimum support class according prevalence (.e., frequency \(c_i\) transactions). Following minimum class support suggested CBA Liu et al. (2000), use $$minsupp_i = minsupp_t   \frac{supp(c_i)}{max(supp(C))},$$ \(max(supp(C))\) support majority class. Therefore, defined minimum support used majority class minimum support scaled less prevalent classes, giving chance produce reasonable number rules. named numeric vector support value class can also specified.
